x: The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949 under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948. 1 July 1955 is SBI, and 19 July 1969 the bank nationalisation.
t: Match each date to its event.

x: Option C is incorrect: LIC was formed on 1 September 1956 under the LIC Act, 1956, by merging over 240 insurers and societies. 19 July 1969 is the date 14 commercial banks were nationalised.
t: Separate the 1956 LIC date from the 1969 bank nationalisation date.
o: The nationalisation of LIC involved merging over 240 private insurers and societies.
LIC was nationalised through the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956.

x: Both are true: RRBs began on 2 October 1975, and Prathama Bank (Moradabad) was the first. Naming the first bank does not explain the start date, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an example explains a date.

x: Both are true: in 1969, 14 banks with deposits of ₹50 crore or more were nationalised, and in 1980 six more with ₹200 crore or more.
t: Recall the 1969 and 1980 thresholds.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: In 1969, 14 major commercial banks with deposits of at least ₹50 crore were nationalised.
Statement B: In 1980, six more commercial banks with deposits of at least ₹200 crore were nationalised.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: All three are correct: NABARD came in 1982 (Sivaraman Committee), SIDBI in 1990 for MSMEs, and the Narasimham I report in 1991.
t: Arrange the institutions in time order.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. NABARD was established in 1982 under the B. Sivaraman Committee recommendations.
II. SIDBI was established in 1990 as the principal financial institution for promotion and financing of MSMEs.
III. The Narasimham Committee I report was submitted in 1991.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The order is SBI (1955), LIC (1956), the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act (1959) and the nationalisation of 14 banks (1969). The answer is A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the milestones in time order.

x: In 1993 New Bank of India merged into PNB, in 2017 five associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank into SBI, in 2020 ten PSBs into four, and from 2021 came the strategic disinvestment policy. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each merger to its year.

x: The Banking Regulation Act was passed in 1949, the same year the RBI was nationalised.
t: Recall the 1949 banking events.

x: Both are true: SBI was formed by taking over the Imperial Bank of India, under the SBI Act, 1955. The Act is the legal basis, not the reason for the takeover, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a legal basis explains an action.

x: All six were nationalised in 1980: Andhra Bank, Corporation Bank, New Bank of India, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Punjab & Sind Bank and Vijaya Bank.
t: Recall the six banks of 1980.

x: The SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959, brought eight banks linked to princely states under SBI.
t: Recall the number 8.

x: The 14 banks were nationalised under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1969.
t: Match each event to its Act.

x: Both are true: the NABARD Act was passed in 1981 and NABARD set up in 1982, and the EXIM Bank also came in 1982.
t: Discriminate the Act year from the start year.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: NABARD was established through the NABARD Act, 1981.
Statement B: EXIM Bank was set up in 1982.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: Both are true and R explains A: the 1991 Narasimham I report launched banking reforms precisely through its recommendations to admit new private banks and free interest rates.
t: Check whether R gives the content that makes A happen.
s:
Assertion (A): The Narasimham Committee I (1991) report began banking-sector reforms in India.
Reason (R): The report recommended entry of private banks and deregulation of interest rates.

x: The loss-making New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank in 1993, the first merger of two nationalised banks.
t: Recall the 1993 merger.

x: All five are correct: OBC and United Bank went into PNB, Syndicate into Canara, and Andhra and Corporation into Union Bank. Allahabad Bank went into Indian Bank.
t: Recall the 2020 mergers.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2020 public sector bank consolidation:
I. Oriental Bank of Commerce merged into Punjab National Bank.
II. United Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank.
III. Syndicate Bank merged into Canara Bank.
IV. Andhra Bank merged into Union Bank of India.
V. Corporation Bank merged into Union Bank of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: OBC and United Bank went into PNB, Syndicate into Canara, Andhra and Corporation into Union Bank, and Allahabad into Indian Bank. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each bank to its new owner.

x: The 2020 mergers cut the number of public sector banks to 12, from 27 in 2017.
t: Recall the number 12.

x: Both are true: Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank both merged into Bank of Baroda in 2019. One merger does not explain the other, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two parallel events explain each other.

x: The Bank of Baroda merger with Dena and Vijaya Banks took effect on 1 April 2019. The 2020 mergers took effect on 1 April 2020.
t: Discriminate 2019 from 2020.

x: The Basel Committee was first called the Committee on Banking Regulations and Supervisory Practices. Basel I (1988) set capital adequacy, Basel II (2004) added supervision and market discipline, and Basel III (2010) strengthened capital. The answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Arrange the Basel accords in time order.

x: Both are true: the Basel Committee arose from currency and banking turmoil, and the failure of Bankhaus Herstatt (1974) was the main trigger. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the trigger explains the setting up.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Basel Committee was set up at the end of 1974, not 1975. Its secretariat is at the Bank for International Settlements in Basel.
t: Recall the year, 1974.

x: Both are true: growth is mainly quantitative, a rise in output, while development is broader and normative, covering living standards and well-being.
t: Discriminate growth from development.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Economic growth is mainly a quantitative concept concerned with a rise in actual output.
Statement B: Economic development is a broader and normative concept involving better living standards and overall socio-economic well-being.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: Both are true: GDP and GNP growth measure economic growth because growth is a quantitative rise in output. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the definition explains the measure.

x: Promoting financial literacy is an aim of financial inclusion, so people know about and use financial services. The other options are the reverse of inclusion.
t: Find the option that widens access.

x: Financial inclusion aims to bring financial services to the poor. The 'only' options name groups that already have access.
t: Watch for 'only' narrowing the group.

x: Financial inclusion expands banking into underserved and rural areas, where access is weakest.
t: Find the option that widens access.

x: Financial inclusion aims to give weaker sections access to credit.
t: Find the option that widens access.

x: Both are true: the Rangarajan Committee on Financial Inclusion set out a strategy, and its final report came on 4 January 2008. A report date does not explain a focus, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a date explains a focus.

x: Both are true: the FSDC oversees the financial system as a whole because it is the apex forum for financial stability and development. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the apex role explains the task.

x: Both are true: financial inclusion means access to formal financial services, and exclusion means lacking that access.
t: Discriminate inclusion from exclusion.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Financial inclusion provides access to formal financial services.
Statement B: Financial exclusion is associated with a lack of access to formal financial services.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: A is true and B is false: having a bank account is a sign of inclusion, while being unable to get credit is a sign of exclusion.
t: Discriminate inclusion from exclusion.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A bank account is associated with financial inclusion.
Statement B: Credit constraints are associated with financial inclusion.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: B is true and A is false: the FSDC covers financial stability and development and also financial literacy and inclusion. 'Only' makes A false.
t: Watch for 'only' narrowing the scope.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The FSDC focuses only on financial stability and development.
Statement B: The FSDC also focuses on financial literacy and financial inclusion.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: I and II are correct: inclusion eases payments and remittances and widens insurance. III is false because inclusion increases financial security.
t: Watch for 'reduce' replacing 'promote'.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Financial inclusion facilitates payments and remittances through the formal financial system.
II. Financial inclusion promotes access to insurance.
III. Financial inclusion seeks to reduce financial security.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: I, II and III are correct: small finance banks lend to small businesses, small and marginal farmers, and rural entrepreneurs. Regulators are FSDC members, not borrowers.
t: Find the group that is not a borrower.
s:
Consider the following statements about the credit provided by Small Financing Banks:
I. Small business units are beneficiaries.
II. Small and marginal farmers are beneficiaries.
III. Entrepreneurs, particularly in rural areas, are beneficiaries.
IV. Financial-sector regulators are identified as beneficiaries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The Committee on Financial Inclusion was chaired by C. Rangarajan, set up on 26 June 2006, and reported on 4 January 2008. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: Inclusion means access to formal finance for the poor, exclusion means lacking insurance and credit, the 2006 committee was chaired by C. Rangarajan and the FSDC by the Union Finance Minister, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each concept or body to its defining feature.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Financial inclusion
(b) Financial exclusion
(c) Committee on Financial Inclusion (2006)
(d) Financial Stability and Development Council

List-II
(i) Lack of access to insurance and credit
(ii) Access to formal financial services for the poor
(iii) Chaired by Dr. C. Rangarajan
(iv) Chaired by the Union Finance Minister

Options

x: Three are signs of exclusion: little or no banking access, difficulty getting credit, and limited payment facilities. Financial security is an outcome of inclusion.
t: Sort into inclusion and exclusion.

x: The FSDC's members include the heads of the financial regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA), among others.
t: Recall the FSDC's members.

x: The Union Finance Minister chairs the FSDC. The regulators are members, and Rangarajan chaired the financial inclusion committee.
t: Recall who chairs the FSDC.

x: NABARD stands for National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. Watch for the trap words 'Research', 'Bureau' and 'Board'.
t: Expand the short name.

x: Option A is incorrect: NABARD was set up in 1982 under the NABARD Act (Act 61 of 1981), with its head office in Mumbai. 1975 is the year RRBs began.
t: Discriminate the NABARD and RRB years.

x: NABARD mainly refinances other institutions, RRBs lend directly in rural areas, State Land Development Banks give long-term farm loans and SIDBI is the principal institution for MSMEs, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Match each institution to its main role.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) NABARD
(b) Regional Rural Banks
(c) State Land Development Banks
(d) SIDBI

List-II
(i) Direct rural banking and credit
(ii) Principal financial institution for MSMEs
(iii) Mainly refinances institutions
(iv) Long-term rural/agricultural loans

x: The order is RRBs (1975), NABARD (1982), the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (1992–93) and the Kisan Credit Card (1998). The answer is B, C, D, A.
t: Arrange the rural credit milestones in time order.

x: Both are true: NABARD was set up during the Sixth Plan, and it is the apex bank for farm refinance. Its role does not explain its timing, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a role explains a date.

x: I, II and IV are correct: NABARD finances both agriculture and rural development. III is false because of 'alone'.
t: Watch for 'alone' narrowing the scope.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. NABARD is associated with financing agriculture.
II. NABARD is associated with financing rural development.
III. NABARD is associated with financing agriculture alone.
IV. NABARD is associated with both agriculture and rural development.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All four get NABARD refinance: scheduled commercial banks, RRBs, State Land Development Banks and State Cooperative Banks.
t: Recall whom NABARD refinances.

x: Both are true: RIDF is the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund, set up in 1995–96 and run by NABARD.
t: Recall the RIDF year.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: RIDF stands for Rural Infrastructure Development Fund.
Statement B: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund was created in 1995–96.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: RIDF finances rural infrastructure, such as roads, irrigation and bridges. Long-term farm loans come from Land Development Banks.
t: Match each fund to its purpose.

x: Both are true: NABARD works mainly as a refinancing apex bank for banks that lend to farmers, and RRBs serve rural and semi-urban areas directly.
t: Contrast NABARD's refinance role with the direct lending of RRBs.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: NABARD mainly provides refinance rather than direct credit to farmers.
Statement B: Regional Rural Banks are associated with rural and semi-urban banking.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

x: Option A is incorrect: RRBs lend mainly to small and marginal farmers, farm labourers and rural artisans, not to large industry.
t: Find the borrower outside the rural poor.

x: Both are true: NABARD is the apex body for rural finance because its main job is refinancing the banks that lend in rural areas. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the function explains the apex status.

x: I, II and III are correct: RRBs bank in rural and semi-urban areas, gather rural savings and support commercial banks. IV is false because RRBs do give institutional farm credit.
t: Watch for 'do not' reversing a role.

x: The first RRB was Prathama Bank, set up at Moradabad (UP) on 2 October 1975 and sponsored by Syndicate Bank, and RRBs serve rural and semi-urban areas, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the basic facts about the first RRB.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First Regional Rural Bank
(b) Location of the first RRB
(c) Sponsor bank of the first RRB
(d) Areas where RRBs provide banking services

List-II
(i) Rural and semi-urban areas
(ii) Syndicate Bank
(iii) Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh
(iv) Prathama Bank
